criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The mission goal, objectives, requirements, and user needs (GBRMPA, AIMS, CSIRO, BoM) are exceptionally clear, quantifiable, and supported with appropriate literature citations.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days instead of

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: The plan includes a well-structured Gantt chart, task descriptions tied directly to mission requirements, robust risk management with triggers and contingencies, and a comprehensive table of planned information sources.

evidence.quote: The main risks and the planned responses are listed in Table 1.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Presents rigorous hand calculations for a sun-synchronous orbit, verified against STK, alongside critical physical interpretation identifying a key coverage trade-off that feeds back into the project plan.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The presentation is outstanding. Formatting, tables, and Gantt chart are clean and legible; language is professional; and referencing follows IEEE style impeccably with matching in-text citations.

evidence.quote: [7] J. R. Wertz, D. F. Everett, and J. J. Puschell, Eds., Space Mission Engineering: The New SMAD. Hawthorne, CA, USA: Microcosm Press, 2011.

overall: An exceptional preliminary report that addresses all requirements thoroughly. The mission rationale is compelling, the project plan and risk contingencies are mature, and the preliminary orbital calculations demonstrate meaningful progress.

feedback.summary: You submitted an exceptional preliminary report that met all task requirements to an advanced standard. Your mission concept, detailed project plan, and preliminary orbital calculations provide a strong foundation for Part 2.
next_steps: Implement the planned coverage trade-off study to address the swath width versus revisit time constraint identified in your preliminary orbital analysis.
Incorporate the detailed payload mass, power, and data volume budgets into your next iteration to build upon the preliminary progress.
Maintain the professional IEEE citation standard and high-quality tabular formatting throughout the final report.

criteria.C1: You achieved the Accomplished level by presenting clear, quantifiable goals, requirements, and user needs (GBRMPA, AIMS, CSIRO, BoM) directly supported by relevant literature.
criteria.C2: You achieved the Accomplished level with a robust Gantt chart, explicit requirement-linked tasks, credible information sources, and strong risk contingencies in Table 1.
criteria.C3: You achieved the Accomplished level by pairing rigorous hand calculations for a sun-synchronous orbit with STK verification and insightful physical interpretation regarding swath width.
criteria.C4: You achieved the Accomplished level through professional layout, clear tables, polished technical language, and impeccable IEEE referencing with matching in-text citations.
